stemBlocks.value: The graph represents y = -x² + 4x + 5. (a) State the x-intercepts. (b) State the y-intercept. (c) State the maximum value and the value of x at which it occurs. (d) Write the equation of the axis of symmetry.
Think first: The curve opens downwards because of the negative x² term, so its turning point is a maximum.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p149-q02 from workbook page 149.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read where the curve crosses the x-axis.

contentBlocks.value: The curve meets the axis at x = -1 and x = 5, confirmed by -x² + 4x + 5 = 0 → x² − 4x − 5 = 0 → (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0

solutionSteps.instruction: Read where the curve crosses the y-axis.
Locate the highest point of the curve.

contentBlocks.value: The vertex sits midway between the roots, at x = (-1 + 5)/2 = 2, and y = -(2)² + 4(2) + 5 = 9
The vertical line through the vertex

strategyBlocks.value: Read where the curve meets each axis, locate the highest point of the curve, and use the symmetry of the parabola to write the axis of symmetry.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x-intercepts at x = -1 and x = 5  (b) y-intercept 5  (c) Maximum value 9, occurring at x = 2  (d) Axis of symmetry x = 2.

whyThisWorks.value: The sign of the x² coefficient decides the shape: negative means the arms point downwards, so the turning point is the highest value the function reaches. A parabola is symmetric, so the vertex always sits exactly halfway between the two x-intercepts — that gives the x-value of the maximum without any further algebra, and substituting it gives the maximum value itself.

commonErrors.misconception: Calling 9 the maximum point rather than the maximum value — the point is (2, 9).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Calling 9 the maximum point rather than the maximum value — the point is (2, 9).

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the y-intercept as an x-value.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the y-intercept as an x-value.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming the axis of symmetry is the y-axis whenever the curve looks central on the grid.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming the axis of symmetry is the y-axis whenever the curve looks central on the grid.

examTip.value: Halve the sum of the two roots to find the axis of symmetry — it is quicker and safer than reading the vertex position off the grid.
